issues.sym: A creak or squeak from the front wheels at low speed and over speed bumps, or a clunk from the front end on rough pavement.
issues.why: The ball joints in the front upper control arms wear out early, often after water gets past the seal and washes out the grease.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Worn upper control arms are usually replaced as complete parts, followed by an alignment.

issues.t: Front lateral link bolts can loosen (recalls 21V-835, 23V-235)
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from the front suspension, a change in steering feel, or the car pulling to one side.
issues.why: Fasteners holding the front lateral links to the subframe may not have been tightened properly and can work loose.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both recalls and have the fasteners inspected. Stop driving if you hear new clunks or the steering feels off.

issues.t: Brake caliper bolts may be loose (recall 21V-387)
issues.sym: A grinding or scraping noise from a wheel, or reduced braking.
issues.why: Caliper mounting bolts may not have been fully tightened, letting the caliper shift and touch the wheel rim.
issues.next: Have the recall inspection done right away and avoid driving if you hear grinding from a wheel.

issues.sym: The car will not wake up or unlock, the screen stays dark, or a message says the low-voltage battery needs service.
issues.why: Earlier cars use a small lead-acid 12V battery that runs the computers and door locks, and it can wear out within a few years.
issues.next: Replace the 12V battery as soon as the warning appears so you are not stranded. Later cars moved to a lithium low-voltage battery.

issues.t: Heat pump loses cabin heat and defrost (recall 22V-050)
issues.sym: No warm air from the vents in freezing weather, and the windshield will not clear.
issues.why: A software error could open a valve in the heat pump and trap refrigerant, which cuts heating and defrost.
issues.next: Make sure the over-the-air recall update is installed. Do not drive if you cannot clear the windshield.

issues.t: Sudden braking with no obstacle (phantom braking)
issues.sym: The car warns of a collision or brakes hard for no visible reason, often while using Autopilot or traffic-aware cruise control.
issues.why: The driver-assist cameras and software can mistake shadows, overpasses or oncoming traffic for a hazard. NHTSA investigated 2021-2022 cars, and a 2021 software version was recalled for false warnings and braking.
issues.next: Keep software updated and confirm recall 21V-846 is complete. Stay alert with your foot ready on the accelerator, and report events to Tesla and NHTSA.

issues.t: Backup camera image missing or delayed
issues.sym: The screen stays blank or shows the rear view late after shifting into reverse.
issues.why: Repeated opening and closing of the trunk can damage the camera wiring harness, and some software versions on Autopilot computer 2.5 delayed the image (recall 22V-169).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open camera recalls. Until it is fixed, check mirrors and look behind you before backing up.

issues.t: Water in the trunk or taillights
issues.sym: Damp carpet or standing water in the trunk well, or fog inside the taillight lenses after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water runs off the trunk lid opening and seals around the trunk and taillight gaskets on early cars were not always tight.
issues.next: Dry the area to avoid mold and have the seals and taillights checked or resealed.

issues.t: Musty or sour smell from the A/C
issues.sym: A damp, mildew or dirty-sock odor from the vents, strongest when the A/C first starts.
issues.why: Moisture stays on the A/C evaporator after driving and lets mold and bacteria grow, and the cabin filters trap it.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air filters, have the evaporator cleaned, and let the system dry out using the A/C drying setting if available.

issues.t: Front shoulder belt anchor may not be attached (recall 21V-389)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; the belt may feel loose at the upper anchor on the pillar.
issues.why: The front shoulder belt fastener at the B-pillar may not have been connected properly at the factory.
issues.next: Have the recall inspection done before carrying front passengers; the belt may not hold in a crash.

issues.t: Side curtain airbag may be mounted wrong (recall 21V-834)
issues.sym: No warning signs in normal driving.
issues.why: The side curtain airbag may not be fastened to the roof rail correctly, so it could twist and deploy poorly.
issues.next: Check the VIN and have the airbag inspected and resecured under the recall.

issues.t: Touchscreen lags or reboots while fast charging (recall 22V-296)
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, lags or restarts, which can take out the backup camera, gear display and windshield controls.
issues.why: The infotainment processor could overheat during or before fast charging on certain software versions.
issues.next: Install the latest software update. If the screen goes dark while driving, pull over safely and wait for it to restart.

issues.t: Hood may not warn when unlatched (recall 24V-554)
issues.sym: No hood-open alert even though the front trunk is not fully latched; the hood could open while driving.
issues.why: The hood latch switch may fail to detect that the hood was opened and not closed.
issues.next: Push the front trunk lid fully closed every time and have the latch recall repair done.

issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, often at low speed or after parking maneuvers, with a steering warning on screen.
issues.why: Repeated low-speed maneuvering could overstress the power steering circuit board on cars with older software.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and make sure the software is updated. Pull over safely if steering gets heavy while driving.

issues.t: High-voltage battery disconnect may be defective (recall 23V-434)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power or a warning that the car cannot be driven.
issues.why: The pyrotechnic battery disconnect device that cuts high-voltage power could be faulty.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have it repaired; a car that loses drive power should be pulled over and towed.

issues.sym: One or both taillights flicker or stay dark.
issues.why: A fault on some early-build 2023 cars could keep the taillights from lighting at times.
issues.next: Make sure the software update is installed and walk around the car to check your lights.

issues.t: Rearview camera image lost from a computer board short (recall 25V-002)
issues.sym: Backup camera shows nothing when in reverse, sometimes along with other camera features failing.
issues.why: A circuit board in the car's computer can short out.
issues.next: Have the computer checked under the recall and look behind you carefully before backing up until it is fixed.

issues.t: Battery pack contactor failure and loss of drive power (recall 25V-690)
issues.sym: A warning message followed by sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: Contactors inside the high-voltage battery pack may fail and cut power to the motors.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have the battery contactors serviced. If power drops, steer to a safe spot and stop.

issues.t: Seat back fasteners may be loose (recall 25V-410)
issues.sym: A seat back that rocks, creaks or feels loose.
issues.why: Fasteners holding the seat back may not have been tightened properly at the factory.
issues.next: Have the seat fasteners checked under the recall; a loose seat back may not protect you in a crash.
